text.p: Swiss shares recovered from a weak bias in late trade but fell off of their highest levels to close lower after Wall Street posted early losses.

After briefly falling beneath the resistance line around 3,820 points, the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) began a gradual rise towards the end of the session. But a weaker Dow Jones marred sentiment again, a dealer said.
"If the Dow Jones goes up, or at least keeps above 6,200 points, we may see buying interest in Zurich on Monday", he added.
The SMI closed 20.7 points, or 0.54 percent, lower at 3,839.3 and the all share SPI fell 10.55 points to 2,454.68.
Volume was comparatively light, a dealer said.
Utility and energy group Electrowatt stood out among blue chips, adding 1.7 percent to end at 527 francs.
Dealers said there were recurring rumours that CS Holding, which owns 44.9 percent in Electrowatt, may be preparing to partially or wholly sell its stake before the year's end.
CS Holding, which declined to comment on market rumours, eased 0.75 francs to 135.

Stocks of chemical group Clariant were depressed by profit taking. They fell nearly two percent to 561 francs after a recent steep rise following the announcement this week of its merger with Hoechst's speciality chemical business.
Most-active Roche certificates slid 60 francs to 9,925. Sandoz gave up more than one percent to 1,506.
Among financials, insurer Winterthur lost 11 francs to 755. UBS bearer shares fell three francs to 1,180.
ABB were lower but kept losses in check amid good buying interest. The shares dropped six francs to 1,607. Sulzer added two francs to close at 741.
